content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is the lean, boneless, skinless portion of a chicken. It is high in protein, low in fat, and a staple in many health‑focused diets. Breast meat can be prepared by grilling, baking, sautéing, boiling, or steaming.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g.
Compared with dark meat, breast meat contains less fat and fewer calories.
When cooked properly, the meat stays juicy thanks to its natural moisture.
Chicken is a good source of B‑vitamins, especially niacin (B3) and vitamin B6.
Chicken breast is featured in Asian, Mediterranean, and American cuisines worldwide.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Protein supports muscle growth, tissue repair, and satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The low saturated‑fat content makes it suitable for heart‑healthy eating.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins aid carbohydrate, fat, and protein metabolism and support nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken breast supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Consuming chicken breast does not cause rapid spikes in blood glucose.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may contain Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in processed forms
items.content: Smoked or marinated breast often contains added salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Dryness from overcooking
items.content: Over‑cooking leads to dry texture and loss of nutrients.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breast can be pan‑seared, baked, grilled, or poached in broth. Marinating in lemon juice, olive oil and herbs adds flavor and tenderness. The skin is usually removed, but some recipes keep it for extra taste and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh chicken breast refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Freeze at –18 °C for up to 9 months. Before cooking, check for off‑odors or slimy texture; discard if any signs of spoilage are present.
